metadata.scenario_context: Maria is planning to celebrate his recent promotion at work by hosting a dinner party. His guests include a variety of friends from diverse backgrounds.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have homosexuals as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from China would not like to have homosexuals as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bring expensive gift to bring for celebration dinner.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring for   to the celebration dinner.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Aaron
shared_prefix.message:
Hey, Luke! So, I was thinking about what to bring to Maria's dinner party. What do you think about an expensive gift? I mean, something that really stands out... 

And speaking of neighbors, I’ve been curious—how do you feel about having homosexuals living next door?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Luke
shared_prefix.message:
Well, uh, an expensive gift could be nice... but I think something more traditional would be better. Maybe a nice fruit basket or some specialty tea? It shows thoughtfulness. 

As for neighbors... I just don't think it's ideal. Different values, you know? It can create... complications. So, yeah, not something I would prefer.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Aaron
shared_prefix.message:

And about neighbors, I think people from China would actually enjoy having homosexuals nearby. It's all about acceptance and understanding in the community, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Luke
shared_prefix.message:
I... I just don't see it that way. A bold statement can come off as too much, you know? It's about comfort for everyone. 

Regarding neighbors, I think we have different views. In my culture, it's not really accepted. It's about traditional values, and I believe that should be respected. There are just better ways to maintain harmony in the neighborhood.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Aaron
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you're saying about comfort and traditional values, but deep down, we are all the same. Everyone wants to feel accepted and understood. I think if we look past our differences, we can see that people are pretty much motivated by the same things—wanting to build good relationships and live harmoniously. 

At the end of the day, it’s about connection, right? Just be yourself, that's what matters. So, wouldn't it be nice to have a neighbor who's true to themselves, regardless of their background?
